text:
carmen: FYI ran a bunch of perf traces on the tool-call path. Requests that trigger function/tool calls show decode batching collapse — latency 2-3x and tiny batches after the pause. attaching pprof+nvprof snippets.
ryan: curious — is this the stop-token induced pause or an external I/O wait? :thinking:
carmen: looks like both. stop token emitted -> runtime pauses decode loop while tool executes -> we end up flushing partially formed batches and then later tiny batches form when tool returns. flamegraph: long idle in scheduler between kernel launches.
priya: that suggests our batch formation/queue policy isn't accounting for expected pauses. current config is size_or_time with soft_wait_ms=2 and token_budget_target=128 — too aggressive for tool-heavy requests.
alex: also check kernel selection overhead. switching kernels for different seq lengths and quant modes adds CPU/GPU sync points; that plus pause could amplify tail.
mike: I saw similar in earlier replay. when KV cache get/put happens around a pause we sometimes rebind buffers which forces a context sync.
infra-bot: trace 1763501234-0 uploaded -> /traces/1763501234/trace.json (pprof: flamegraph.svg, nvprof: timeline.nvvp)
ryan: can you paste the pprof hot path? small excerpt is fine.
carmen: hot path snippet:
```
Scheduler::poll_batches -> BatchManager::finalize_batch -> Decoder::dispatch_kernel -> cudaStreamSynchronize
// then long gap while ToolInvoker::run
```
priya: ok so sync points inside dispatch_kernel. two potential levers: (1) prevent finalize_batch from doing costly kernel selection on paused batches, (2) change queue policy to hold paused requests in a separate pending set and continue forming batches of non-paused requests.
alex: for (1) we could add a lightweight kernel decision fast-path for paused tokens: use last_chosen_kernel unless seq_len delta > threshold.
mike: for (2) we should try a triage queue: active, paused(toolcall), warming. active batches get normal token_budget_target; paused ones tagged and not included in size/count triggers until tool returns or soft_wait expires.
priya: propose experiments (low effort first):
- A: increase soft_wait_ms from 2 -> 8, token_budget_target 128 -> 192 (expect fewer small batches)
- B: enable "pause_cohorting" (hold paused requests out of main batch queue) + token_budget_target 128
- C: kernel fast-path: skip heavy selection when is_paused=true
each run with same synthetic tool latency 200ms and mixed seq lengths.
ryan: add metric: p50/p95 batch size, per-token latency, kernel switch count, cuda sync count.
carmen: I'll run A+B on a small canary cluster tomorrow morning and collect traces. anyone want to own C (kernel fast-path)?
alex: i'll take C. low-risk change, can gate behind feature flag.
mike: I'll add an eval to the repro harness to emit KV cache ops around pause to see if rebinds correlate.
priya: reproduction command for reference:
```
./tools/run_perf --model gpt-3.8-q4 --mix "short:0.6,long:0.4" --tool-latency 200 --duration 10m --trace-id 1763501234
```
carmen: thanks. one more thought: structured output (JSON outputs w/ stop-token heuristics) seems to cause earlier stop emission which confuses token_budget heuristics. might need to detect structured mode and raise token_budget_target automatically.ryan: (note) we don't have a bryan in thread, ignore
ryan: good point — add structured_output flag to batching config so generation that uses deterministic stop tokens gets a higher budget by default.
priya: summarize next steps: carmen -> run A+B + upload traces; alex -> implement kernel fast-path behind flag; mike -> KV rebind traces; i'll update perf dashboard to show sync counts. We'll reconvene after traces.
carmen: cool. I'll post results link here when done :thumbsup:
